title: Chess Quick Start (Super Beginner)(en,skill)
details: Ultra-simple chess rules and first steps for total beginners. Short, friendly flashcards: one tiny rule + one common mistake. Built to reach confident Beginner level fast.

modules.moduleDescription: Super simple rules: setup, how pieces move, special moves, and basic draws. Built for total beginners (58 cards).

cards.title: 01. Board Corner
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Set the board so the bottom-right corner is a light square.
Don’t: Start playing if the corner is dark.

cards.title: 02. White Moves First
cards.cardDescription:
Do: White always moves first.
Don’t: Take two turns in a row.

cards.title: 03. One Move Only
cards.cardDescription:
Do: On your turn, make one move (castling counts as one).
Don’t: Move two pieces in one turn.

cards.title: 04. Queen on Her Color
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Put the white queen on d1 (light) and the black queen on d8 (dark).
Don’t: Swap king and queen.

cards.title: 05. Kings Start Here
cards.cardDescription:
Do: White king starts on e1; black king starts on e8.
Don’t: Put the king on d-file.

cards.title: 06. Rooks in Corners
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Put rooks in the corners.
Don’t: Put rooks next to the king.

cards.title: 07. Knights Next to Rooks
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Knights go next to rooks.
Don’t: Place knights on bishop squares.

cards.title: 08. Bishops Next to Knights
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bishops go next to knights.
Don’t: Put bishops on the edge by mistake.

cards.title: 09. Pawns in Front
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pawns fill the whole second rank (white) and seventh rank (black).
Don’t: Leave gaps in the pawn line.

cards.title: 10. Capture Means Replace
cards.cardDescription:
Do: When you capture, your piece goes on that square and the enemy piece is removed.
Don’t: Keep both pieces on one square.

cards.title: 11. Can’t Capture Your Own
cards.cardDescription:
Do: You can only capture enemy pieces.
Don’t: Capture your own piece.

cards.title: 12. Sliding Pieces Need Space
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Rooks, bishops, and queens need empty squares to slide through.
Don’t: Jump over pieces with them.

cards.title: 13. Knight Jumps
cards.cardDescription:
Do: A knight can jump over pieces.
Don’t: Try to jump with a bishop or rook.

cards.title: 14. Rook Moves Straight
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Rook moves any number of squares straight (up/down/left/right).
Don’t: Move a rook diagonally.

cards.title: 15. Bishop Moves Diagonal
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bishop moves any number of squares diagonally.
Don’t: Move a bishop straight.

cards.title: 16. Bishop Color
cards.cardDescription:
Do: A bishop stays on the same color squares forever.
Don’t: Expect it to switch colors.

cards.title: 17. Queen Moves Like Both
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Queen moves like a rook OR a bishop.
Don’t: Move the queen like a knight.

cards.title: 18. King Moves 1
cards.cardDescription:
Do: King moves 1 square in any direction.
Don’t: Move the king two squares (unless castling).

cards.title: 19. King Can Capture
cards.cardDescription:
Do: King can capture like it moves (1 square).
Don’t: Capture a piece that is protected (king would be in danger).

cards.title: 20. Knights Move in an L
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Knight moves 2 squares then 1 to the side (an L shape).
Don’t: Move a knight in a straight line.

cards.title: 21. Pawn Moves Straight
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pawn moves straight forward (not sideways).
Don’t: Move a pawn backward.

cards.title: 22. Pawn Captures Diagonal
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pawn captures 1 step diagonally forward.
Don’t: Capture straight forward with a pawn.

cards.title: 23. Pawn First Double Step
cards.cardDescription:
Do: A pawn can move 2 squares only from its start square.
Don’t: Move 2 squares after it already moved once.

cards.title: 24. Pawn Blocked
cards.cardDescription:
Do: A pawn cannot move forward if a piece is in front of it.
Don’t: Move a pawn through a piece.

cards.title: 25. En Passant Exists
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If a pawn moves 2 squares and lands next to your pawn, you may capture it right away (special rule).
Don’t: Try it later—it's only right away.

cards.title: 26. Promotion
cards.cardDescription:
Do: When a pawn reaches the last rank, it becomes a new piece (usually a queen).
Don’t: Leave the pawn there without changing it.

cards.title: 27. Promotion Choices
cards.cardDescription:
Do: You may promote to queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
Don’t: Think you must promote only to a queen.

cards.title: 28. What Is Check
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Check means your king can be captured next move.
Don’t: Ignore check and play another move.

cards.title: 29. Fix Check: Move King
cards.cardDescription:
Do: To answer check, you can move your king to a safe square.
Don’t: Move the king onto an attacked square.

cards.title: 30. Fix Check: Capture
cards.cardDescription:
Do: To answer check, you can capture the checking piece (if legal).
Don’t: Capture it if that still leaves your king in danger.

cards.title: 31. Fix Check: Block
cards.cardDescription:
Do: To answer check, you can block a rook/bishop/queen check with a piece.
Don’t: Try to block a knight check (you can’t).

cards.title: 32. Checkmate
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Checkmate = check and there is no legal way to escape.
Don’t: Keep playing after checkmate.

cards.title: 33. You Never Capture the King
cards.cardDescription:
Do: The game ends at checkmate; the king is never taken.
Don’t: Try to “capture the king.”

cards.title: 34. Stalemate
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Stalemate = you have no legal move, but your king is NOT in check (draw).
Don’t: Call it checkmate by mistake.

cards.title: 35. Draw Agreement
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Players can agree to a draw anytime.
Don’t: Keep arguing—just offer/accept politely.

cards.title: 36. Threefold Repetition
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If the same position happens 3 times with the same player to move, a draw can be claimed.
Don’t: Assume it happens automatically in every app.

cards.title: 37. Insufficient Material
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Some endings can’t make mate (like king vs king), so it’s a draw.
Don’t: Think any extra piece always wins.

cards.title: 38. Touch-Move (OTB)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: In many real-board games: if you touch a piece, you must move it (if you can).
Don’t: Grab pieces while thinking.

cards.title: 39. Castling Is King Move
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Castling starts with moving the king (not the rook).
Don’t: Move the rook first and call it castling.

cards.title: 40. Castle Kingside (White)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: White castles kingside: king e1→g1, rook h1→f1.
Don’t: Put the rook on g1.

cards.title: 41. Castle Queenside (White)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: White castles queenside: king e1→c1, rook a1→d1.
Don’t: Put the king on d1.

cards.title: 42. Castle Kingside (Black)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Black castles kingside: king e8→g8, rook h8→f8.
Don’t: Move king to f8.

cards.title: 43. Castle Queenside (Black)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Black castles queenside: king e8→c8, rook a8→d8.
Don’t: Move king to b8.

cards.title: 44. Castle Needs Empty Squares
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Squares between king and rook must be empty to castle.
Don’t: Castle through your own pieces.

cards.title: 45. No Castle If King Moved
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If your king moved earlier, you cannot castle.
Don’t: Try to castle after king walked.

cards.title: 46. No Castle If Rook Moved
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If that rook moved earlier, you cannot castle on that side.
Don’t: Castle with a rook that already moved.

cards.title: 47. No Castle In Check
cards.cardDescription:
Do: You cannot castle while in check.
Don’t: Castle to escape check.

cards.title: 48. No Castle Through Danger
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Your king cannot castle through a square that is attacked.
Don’t: Castle ‘through’ an attacked square.

cards.title: 49. Pieces Attack Squares
cards.cardDescription:
Do: A piece attacks the squares it could capture on.
Don’t: Forget that pawns attack diagonally.

cards.title: 50. Pawns Attack Diagonally
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Even if a pawn is blocked, it still attacks diagonally.
Don’t: Think a blocked pawn attacks nothing.

cards.title: 51. Don’t Leave Pieces Free
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Before you move, see if any of your pieces can be captured for free.
Don’t: Assume the opponent won’t take it.

cards.title: 52. Look for Checks
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Before you move, quickly look: can the opponent give check next?
Don’t: Miss a simple check on your king.

cards.title: 53. Look for Captures
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Before you move, look: can the opponent capture something important next?
Don’t: Only look at your own plan.

cards.title: 54. Look for Hanging Queen
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Always double-check your queen safety.
Don’t: Put your queen where a pawn can take it.

cards.title: 55. Same Square Rule
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Only one piece can be on a square at a time.
Don’t: Stack pieces on one square.

cards.title: 56. Illegal Move Undo
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If a move is illegal, it must be taken back (in real chess rules).
Don’t: Keep playing after an illegal move.

cards.title: 57. Clock Basics
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If you play with a clock, press it after your move.
Don’t: Press the clock before moving.

cards.title: 58. Goal of the Game
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Your goal is to checkmate the enemy king.
Don’t: Win by capturing every piece.

modules.title: 1. Rules & Setup (Ultra Simple)

modules.moduleDescription: Easy opening habits: bring pieces out, play in the middle, and keep your king safe (80 cards).

cards.title: 01. Goal of the Opening
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Build a playable position first.
Don't: Hunting quick mates and ignoring bringing pieces out.

cards.title: 02. Develop Means Move Out
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Knights and bishops usually first.
Don't: Moving the same pawn repeatedly and calling it bringing pieces out.

cards.title: 03. Center First
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Center control gives space and options.
Don't: Playing side pawn moves with no reason.

cards.title: 04. Control vs Occupy
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pieces can also control key squares.
Don't: Overpushing pawns and losing them.

cards.title: 05. Knights Before Bishops (Usually)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Common squares: f3/c3 (or f6/c6).
Don't: Following this blindly when a bishop move is clearly best.

cards.title: 06. One Piece Twice
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Extra moves lose time.
Don't: Chasing pawns with one piece and falling behind.

cards.title: 07. Tempo = Time
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Make moves that help your plan.
Don't: 'Pretty' moves that do nothing.

cards.title: 08. Don’t Bring the Queen Out Early
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bring pieces out minors first.
Don't: Queen adventures for a pawn.

cards.title: 09. Queen Needs Open Lines
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Early positions are crowded.
Don't: Qh5 every game.

cards.title: 10. Castle Early
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Aim to castle by ~move 10.
Don't: Delaying castling while the center opens.

cards.title: 11. Castle Toward Safety
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Safety beats habit.
Don't: Castling into open files.

cards.title: 12. Pawn Shield
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Don’t weaken them for no reason.
Don't: Pushing g- and f-pawns early.

cards.title: 13. Connect Your Rooks
cards.cardDescription:
Do: That means you’re ready to play.
Don't: Leaving pieces on the back rank forever.

cards.title: 14. Active Knight Squares
cards.cardDescription:
Do: They control more squares there.
Don't: Knights on the rim (a3/h3).

cards.title: 15. Knight on the Rim
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Centralize knights.
Don't: Chasing pawns to the edge and getting trapped.

cards.title: 16. Free Your Bishops
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bishops need diagonals.
Don't: Locking bishops behind pawns.

cards.title: 17. Good vs Bad Bishop
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pawn structure matters.
Don't: Trading the good bishop and keeping the bad one.

cards.title: 18. Develop With a Threat (Optional)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Example: Nf3 hits e5.
Don't: Making threats that waste bringing pieces out.

cards.title: 19. Don’t Grab Random Pawns
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bringing pieces out > pawns.
Don't: Taking a 'free pawn' and getting attacked.

cards.title: 20. Open Center When Ahead
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Lines favor activity.
Don't: Opening the center when your king is uncastled.

cards.title: 21. Closed vs Open Center
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Plans depend on pawn structure.
Don't: Same plan in every position.

cards.title: 22. Checks Aren’t Magic
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Checks must improve your position.
Don't: Giving a check and losing that piece.

cards.title: 23. Avoid Empty Checks
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bring pieces out instead.
Don't: Checking for fun.

cards.title: 24. Minimal Pawn Moves
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Usually 1–3 central pawn moves.
Don't: Pushing many pawns and having no pieces out.

cards.title: 25. Don’t Block Your Own Pieces
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Open lines, don’t close them.
Don't: c3+d3+e3 and nothing can move.

cards.title: 26. Develop = Defend
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Often the best defense is bringing pieces out.
Don't: Defending with queen early.

cards.title: 27. Avoid Early King Moves
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Castle instead.
Don't: King walk on move 3.

cards.title: 28. Don’t Lose Castling Rights
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Keep them unmoved until castling.
Don't: Rook move for no reason.

cards.title: 29. Count Attackers/Defenders
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Trades follow math.
Don't: Capturing and losing more back.

cards.title: 30. Blunder-Check Before Every Move
cards.cardDescription:
Do: One scan prevents most losses.
Don't: Only thinking about your own idea.

cards.title: 31. Forcing Moves First
cards.cardDescription:
Do: They limit replies.
Don't: Missing a simple mate.

cards.title: 32. Develop Both Knights
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Get both out early.
Don't: Developing one knight and forgetting the other.

cards.title: 33. Bring Pieces Toward Center
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Centralize for activity.
Don't: Leaving pieces on the back rank.

cards.title: 34. Don’t Chase Pawns With Queen
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Let pieces do the work.
Don't: Queen goes pawn shopping and gets trapped.

cards.title: 35. Trade With Purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Exchanges need a reason.
Don't: Trading because you can.

cards.title: 36. Piece Values (Starter)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Use as a quick guide.
Don't: Values are not absolute.

cards.title: 37. Bishop Pair Idea
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Don’t give them up for no reason.
Don't: Trading a bishop for a pawn early.

cards.title: 38. Knights in Closed Positions
cards.cardDescription:
Do: They jump over blocks.
Don't: Trading your knight and getting stuck.

cards.title: 39. Avoid Early Wing Pawns
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Center first.
Don't: a- and h-pawn pushes with no plan.

cards.title: 40. Don’t Open Lines Near Your King
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Opening files helps attackers.
Don't: Opening the g-file for your other player.

cards.title: 41. Answer Attacks by Developing
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Save time.
Don't: Passive defense moves.

cards.title: 42. Don’t Defend Fake Threats
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Prioritize real dangers.
Don't: Panicking and falling behind.

cards.title: 43. Scholar’s Mate Pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Defend calmly and bring pieces out.
Don't: Ignoring the threat and getting mated.

cards.title: 44. Defend f7/f2
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Watch queen+bishop combos.
Don't: Allowing Qxf7# / Qxf2#.

cards.title: 45. Stop a Pin (Basic)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Sometimes ignore; sometimes break.
Don't: Wasting multiple moves to 'fix' a harmless pin.

cards.title: 46. Castle to Unpin
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Another reason to castle.
Don't: Staying uncastled and suffering pins.

cards.title: 47. What Is an Open File
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Rooks belong there.
Don't: Putting rooks behind your own pawn wall.

cards.title: 48. Rook Activation Timing
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Don’t rush rooks early.
Don't: Rook moves that get chased.

cards.title: 49. Opening Success Metric
cards.cardDescription:
Do: You don’t need a 'winning' opening.
Don't: Overforcing and blundering.

cards.title: 50. Ideas Not Memorization
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Understand why.
Don't: Forget one move and collapse.

cards.title: 51. If You Forget What to Do
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Principles beat random moves.
Don't: Making multiple 'waiting' pawn moves.

cards.title: 52. Do Not Ignore Tactics
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Always scan.
Don't: Playing fast because it’s the opening.

cards.title: 53. Meet Threats With Activity
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Don’t be passive.
Don't: Defending everything and falling behind.

cards.title: 54. Keep Pieces Protected
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Loose pieces drop off.
Don't: Leaving multiple undefended pieces.

cards.title: 55. Loose Pieces Drop Off (LPDO)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Add defenders or move them.
Don't: Ignoring a loose piece and losing it.

cards.title: 56. Don’t Open the Center With King in Middle
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Castle first if possible.
Don't: Trading pawns and exposing your king.

cards.title: 57. Develop One Bishop to a Useful Diagonal
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Prefer active diagonals.
Don't: Bishop out then retreating repeatedly.

cards.title: 58. Avoid Trapping Your Bishop
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Leave it a future.
Don't: 'Solid' pawn chain that kills bishop.

cards.title: 59. Simple White Plan (e4)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Fast bringing pieces out.
Don't: Early queen to h5 with no backup.

cards.title: 60. Simple White Plan (d4)
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Same principles.
Don't: Moving pawns three times to defend d4.

cards.title: 61. Simple Black Plan vs e4
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bring pieces out and fight center.
Don't: Many pawn moves with no pieces.

cards.title: 62. Simple Black Plan vs d4
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Keep it simple.
Don't: Copying without checking tactics.

cards.title: 63. Copycat Warning
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Evaluate threats each move.
Don't: Copying into a trap.

cards.title: 64. When to Play h3/a3
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Don’t play them automatically.
Don't: Losing time.

cards.title: 65. Stop Back Rank Issues Early
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Prevent back rank mates.
Don't: Never giving luft and getting mated.

cards.title: 66. Don’t Push f-pawn Early
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Move it only with a plan.
Don't: f-pawn push opening king lines.

cards.title: 67. Fianchetto Basics
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Needs a solid setup.
Don't: Fianchetto then opening your king.

cards.title: 68. Avoid Random Sacrifices
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Material matters for beginners.
Don't: 'Attack' with one piece.

cards.title: 69. Attack With More Pieces
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Bring pieces first.
Don't: One-piece attack that gets shut down.

cards.title: 70. Choose Safe Squares
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Stability matters.
Don't: Moving to a square attacked by a pawn.

cards.title: 71. Watch Pawn Attacks
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Count pawn attacks.
Don't: Placing a piece on a square a pawn can hit next.

cards.title: 72. Don’t Overextend Pawns
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Pawns can’t go backward.
Don't: Pawn pushes that become weak.

cards.title: 73. Keep Your King Hidden
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Safety first.
Don't: Opening files next to your king.

cards.title: 74. Beginner Opening Checklist
cards.cardDescription:
Do: If yes, you’re fine.
Don't: Starting an attack before checklist is met.

cards.title: 75. Don’t Trade Your Center Pawns Too Early
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Trade when you’re developed and safe.
Don't: Opening lines while undeveloped.

cards.title: 76. Use Development to Gain Space
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Space limits other player.
Don't: Space without bringing pieces out is useless.

cards.title: 77. Avoid Early Piece Traps
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Keep escape squares.
Don't: Bishop/knight goes out and gets trapped by pawns.

cards.title: 78. Bring Queen Out After Pieces
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Queen joins later.
Don't: Queen out early becomes a target.

cards.title: 79. When You’re Ahead, Simplify
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Make the game easier.
Don't: Keeping complications and blundering back.

cards.title: 80. When You’re Behind, Keep Pieces
cards.cardDescription:
Do: Complications create chances.
Don't: Trading into a lost endgame.

modules.title: 2. Opening Principles for New Players
